title: Fix ignore label being included in foreground intensity statistics
author: qinxwew
text:
Fixes #3055.
## Problem
`DatasetFingerprintExtractor.collect_foreground_intensities` builds the foreground mask as `segmentation[0] > 0`, so voxels carrying the `ignore` label are counted as foreground when computing the intensity statistics. For datasets where `ignore` covers large regions this heavily skews the mean/median/percentiles/std — in the CT example from the issue the computed mean was -321 HU with `percentile_99_5` = 701 HU, while the true foreground is ~-40 HU with the 99.5th percentile around 100 HU. The corrupted statistics propagate into the fingerprint and from there into normalization and planning.
## Fix

title: Install the SIGUSR1 handler again at every epoch start; torch.compile can take it away
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
When Triton compiles kernels in the training process (torch.compile with a cold cache), its LLVM installs native
handlers for SIGUSR1, SIGTERM, SIGUSR2 and others. The SIGUSR1 one swallows the signal, so the graceful stop at the
next epoch boundary never happened and the job ran into its time limit. signal.getsignal() keeps returning our
handler, so the only fix is to set it again. Reproduced with torch 2.8.0/Triton 3.4 and torch 2.14/Triton 3.8: the
OS-level handler points into libtriton.so after the first compile, and a signal sent mid-training was ignored. With
this change the same cold-cache run stops at the next epoch boundary. A signal that arrives during the first epoch,
while the kernels are compiled, can still be lost.

title: Write checkpoints as safetensors; keep reading .pth checkpoints
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
A .pth checkpoint is a pickle, and torch.load(..., weights_only=False) runs any code it contains. nnU-Net now
writes checkpoint_final, checkpoint_best and checkpoint_latest as .safetensors: a JSON header plus raw tensor
bytes. The checkpoint holds the same dict as before. Tensors are stored as tensors (shared ones once); all
other state (logging, init args, plans, ...) is typed JSON kept in a uint8 tensor, because the safetensors
header is capped at 100 MB. Loading returns the same values with the same types. The file is written one
tensor at a time through a temporary name, so the whole state never has to sit on the CPU at once and a killed
process never leaves a truncated checkpoint. The format is described in nnunetv2/utilities/checkpoints.py.
 * checkpoint_final no longer contains optimizer_state and grad_scaler_state. Nothing continues from it,
 and the optimizer state is as large as the weights (twice that for Adam). Continuing a finished
 training starts with a fresh optimizer and says so. checkpoint_best and checkpoint_latest keep
 everything.
 * Old .pth checkpoints keep working everywhere: inference, --c, --val, --val_best, -pretrained_weights,
 export. They are loaded exactly as before. A checkpoint name finds the file with the other extension
 if the named one does not exist, so the new default -chk checkpoint_final.safetensors finds an old
 model's checkpoint_final.pth. If both exist, the named one is loaded, with a warning.
 * Continuing an old training loads i…

title: Only let global rank 0 create splits_final.json in DDP (#3064)
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
#3065 publishes splits_final.json by atomic rename, so no process reads a
partially written file. In DDP every rank still entered do_split
concurrently, found no split file and created it itself. Now only global
rank 0 reads or creates the file and broadcasts the splits to the other
ranks. This also removes any dependence on the file being visible on other
nodes of a shared filesystem, and guarantees that all ranks use the same
split, which validation sharding relies on.
The atomic rename stays for independent trainings (e.g. all folds launched
at once), and the temp file is now removed if writing or renaming fails.
do_split is now a collective in DDP and must be called by all ranks;
documented in the changelog under changes that affect custom trainers.

title: Break segmentation resampling ties by geometry, not by label value
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
Resampling a segmentation interpolates each label's indicator and picks a winner per voxel. Whenever an axis
is resampled by an even integer factor, every boundary voxel is an exact 50/50 tie, in plane (512 -> 256) as
much as out of plane. Those ties were decided by label value, and differently on each path:
 * resample_torch (the torch planners) took argmax over ascending labels, so ties always went to the
 smallest label, i.e. background. That eroded foreground systematically and could delete structures one
 voxel thick.
 * Its memefficient_seg_resampling branch assigned with `interp > 0.5`, so a voxel no label claimed kept
 the 0 the result was initialized with, a label the input need not contain ({1, 2} -> 0).
 * The default path (resample_data_or_seg -> batchgenerators' resize_segmentation) had the threshold bug
 too, and its ties went to the largest label. So did the separate-z pass along the anisotropic axis
 whenever order_z != 0.
All of them now take a per-voxel argmax, and a new keyword-only seg_tiebreak settles exact ties:
 'nearest' (default) the nearest neighbour label, where it is one of the tied labels; otherwise the
 smallest tied label. Symmetric in the labels, and what the separate-z path already did.
 'lowest' the smallest tied label; together with memefficient_seg_resampling=False it reproduces the old
 torch results bit for bit.
 'highest' the largest tied label, the closest to the old default path (which nothing reproduces exactly).
resample_data_or_seg…

title: Faster imports and a persistent torch.compile cache
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
- seaborn/pyplot are imported inside LocalLogger.plot_progress_png and sklearn inside
 generate_crossval_split: every inference process imports both modules through nnUNetTrainer but
 never plots or splits (~0.6 s + ~0.2 s per process).
- OptimizedModule checks in nnUNetPredictor go through utilities.helpers.is_optimized_module, which
 does not import torch._dynamo (~0.4 s): a compiled module cannot exist unless it was imported.
- set_default_inductor_cache_dir() before every torch.compile: when TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR is not
 set by the user, the compile cache goes to $XDG_CACHE_HOME (default ~/.cache)/nnunetv2/torchinductor
 instead of /tmp/torchinductor_<user>, which reboots and node-local cluster /tmp wipe, so later
 processes start with a warm cache. A user-set TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR is never changed.
Importing the predictor and the trainer: 1.05 -> 0.72 s. Outputs are unaffected.

title: Compute evaluation metrics from a per-case confusion matrix
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
compute_metrics used to build two boolean masks and run four masked sums
per label/region, i.e. ~15 passes over the volume per class. It now builds
a single confusion matrix per case (lookup table + bincount, processed in
chunks of 2**22 voxels to bound memory) and derives TP/FP/FN/TN for every
label and region from it. Results are identical, including regions and
the ignore label. 512x512x256 with 104 classes: 12.6s -> 0.44s per case.
region_or_label_to_mask and compute_tp_fp_fn_tn are kept unchanged. New
public helpers: compute_confusion_matrix and
compute_tp_fp_fn_tn_for_labels_or_regions. Reference and prediction must
now have identical shapes and integer values; both raise ValueError
otherwise.

title: Support DDP across multiple nodes
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
Every "am I the writer?" guard in nnUNetTrainer used self.local_rank. On one
node that is correct. On n nodes there are n processes with local_rank == 0,
and on a shared filesystem they all write the same training log, the same
checkpoints and the same progress plot, so multi-node DDP was never correct
regardless of how the job was launched.
Separate the two meanings local_rank was carrying:
 local_rank index within the node -> the CUDA device index
 global_rank index within the job -> decides who writes files
 world_size processes in the job
 local_world_size processes on this node
All four come from get_ddp_topology() in nnunetv2/utilities/ddp.py, which
reads the torchrun environment and falls back to dist.get_rank(), the
SLURM/OMPI variables, and finally an exact derivation by all-gathering
hostnames. Every file-write guard in the trainer now uses global_rank.
Three launch paths funnel into one code path in run_training.py: an external
launcher (torchrun, srun, anything speaking its env protocol; single or multi
node), -num_gpus X (nnU-Net spawns the workers itself, single node only, and
emulates the torchrun environment so everything downstream is identical), and
a plain single process. Both nnUNetv2_train and nnUNetv2_train_pretrained go
through it.
Also in this change:
- AllReduceGrad replaces the deprecated AllGatherGrad in the losses. Same
 forward and backward, world_size times less data moved. AllGatherGrad still
 works but warns.
- SIGUSR1 checkpoint-and-exit. The…

title: Memory map every blosc2 read; raise the in-memory store cap to 32 GiB
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
Audited all blosc2.open call sites in the sampling location rework. Six of seven
already passed mmap kwargs; the segmentation read in the extraction pass did not,
and now does. A source level test asserts the invariant for all three modules so
a new read cannot silently drop it.
For the record, the reads and their state:
 foreground_locations locations.b2nd was mapped
 nnunet_dataset load_case data/seg/prev was mapped
 nnunet_dataset get_shape was mapped
 extract_sampling_... <case>_seg.b2nd FIXED
The CSR index arrays are deliberately read eagerly rather than mapped - they are
under 1 MB for TotalSegmentator v2 and every lookup touches them, so page faults
on the hot path would cost more than the memory saved. That trade flips for
datasets with very many classes (100k cases x ~100 present classes would be a
61 MB index per worker), so it is worth revisiting if such a dataset appears.
max_in_memory_bytes 2 GiB -> 32 GiB. to_cframe() transiently holds a second copy,
so this is a ~64 GiB peak. A 32 GiB store is roughly 40 billion coordinates, ~70x
TotalSegmentator v2, which makes the slow on-disk fallback effectively
unreachable in practice. That fallback deliberately stays unmapped: a shared
writable mapping over NFS has no reliable write-back ordering, and blosc2 needs
the final file size up front, which is unknown while cases are still arriving.
Re-verified against the legacy class_locations on Dataset004 after the change:
856,754 coordinates, zero mismatches.

title: Build the sampling location store in RAM and use 32768-element chunks
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
Writing the blosc2 array incrementally to its final path is free on local NVMe
but pathological on a parallel filesystem. blosc2 pays a fixed cost per chunk
there - ~16 ms on GPFS against ~0.09 ms locally - because appending a chunk
rewrites the frame's offset trailer. Measured on GPFS, 7.8 MB of store:
 grow (previous behaviour) 14.83 s
 grow + mmap write 7.56 s
 preallocate + trim 22.93 s
 single asarray() call 9.77 s
 build locally, copy over 2.31 s
 build in RAM, one write 1.12 s
Preallocation, memory-mapped writing and larger flushes were all measured and
none of them fixed it (preallocation was worse, despite going from 16 resizes to
2); the raw filesystem does 800 MB/s at every write size, so the cost is entirely
blosc2's per-chunk traffic. The array is now built without a urlpath and
serialised once in finalize() with to_cframe() + write(). Extrapolated to D351
that is ~1.5 min instead of ~20 min.
Stores too large for RAM spill to the incremental path at max_in_memory_bytes
(2 GiB compressed, so ~4 GiB peak since to_cframe transiently doubles it).
Chunk size goes 8192 -> 32768 (64 blocks per chunk). Also a filesystem decision:
on GPFS that is 3.7x faster to write and 1.8x faster on cold random reads
(131 -> 72 us), for 5% on warm reads. Block size stays 512, which still sets the
compression ratio. 131072 was measured too and is where read cost starts to climb
steeply.
Verified against the legacy class_locations on Dataset004: 856,754 coordinates
across 260 cases, zer…

title: Resample along the anisotropic axis with a gather, and work in float32
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
Preprocessing Dataset003_Liver with -np 32 made no visible progress: every worker sat
in R state burning system time inside resample_data_or_seg. It was not deadlocked,
just so far past the memory bandwidth knee that the first case never finished, and the
progress bar only ticks on the first completion. -np 8 was fine.
Two things in resample_data_or_seg were responsible, both fixed here.
The separate-z out-of-plane step built a full (3, *new_shape) coordinate map: three
int64 mgrid arrays, three float64 arrays derived from them (two temporaries each), and
an np.array() copy of all three - roughly 9x the output volume moved through RAM per
case. But by then the in-plane loop has already brought the other two axes to their
target size, so row_scale and col_scale are exactly 1.0 and two of the three coordinate
maps are identities. Only `axis` is actually resampled. With order_z == 0 (every
shipped plan) a 1d nearest neighbour gather is bit-identical and costs nothing.
order_z != 0 keeps the coordinate map.
The float64 upcast bought no accuracy either. scipy.ndimage accumulates in double
internally whatever dtype the array has, and for order > 1 it forces
spline_filter(..., output=np.float64) on top of that, so upcasting the float32 that
nnU-Net feeds in only doubled the memory. Working precision is now float32, and
reshaped_here follows data.dtype. Input that is not already floating point is still
converted; float64 input is left alone rather than silently downcast.
Measured on…

title: Announce a missing sampling location store once per run, not once per worker
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
The notice was emitted from get_foreground_locations(), which is resolved
lazily - and the first resolution happens inside each dataloader worker, not in
the main process. Workers get their own copy of this module's globals, so the
module-level "already warned" set did not deduplicate across them and the
message was printed once per worker (12 on a typical machine, plus the
validation loader's).
The factory is now silent. announce_missing_store() does the announcing and is
called from nnUNetBaseDataset.__init__, i.e. from the process that builds the
dataset. It stays quiet in child processes and on non-zero DDP ranks, and marks
the folder before the isfile check so the per-case dataset construction in
perform_actual_validation costs nothing after the first.
Resolution of the locations themselves stays lazy.
Verified with a real 1-epoch training on a legacy-format Dataset004 with 12
dataloader workers: the notice appears exactly once, and zero times once the
store exists.
The previous test only constructed two datasets in one process, which is why it
missed this. It is replaced by tests that spawn real worker processes under both
the fork and spawn start methods, plus coverage for the DDP rank guard and for
announcing at construction rather than on first use.
(cherry picked from commit 9bb2b852eeecdd82a8e8c7743f2c505267087855)

title: Clean up the foreground sampling location store
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
Move the store into a fg_sampling/ subdirectory of the configuration folder.
Placing it among the cases required three separate prefix guards (both
get_identifiers implementations and infer_dataset_class), a reserved-prefix
rule in the user-facing format docs, and a test to police it. Directories are
invisible to subfiles() and to the os.listdir + suffix scans, so all of that
goes away and case names are unconstrained again. Rebuilds now rmtree the
directory instead of unlinking a hard-coded file list, which also clears
leftovers of a store written by a different version.
Stop wasting the pkl read on the migration path. extract_case fetched
properties['present_labels'], which a legacy dataset does not have - but the
unpickle still materialized the whole old class_locations dict first (18.26 GB
on TotalSegmentator v2) and returned nothing. That dict already implies the
answer: a class is empty exactly when none of its labels are present, so a
label can be ruled out iff it appears in an empty entry and in no non-empty
one. Conservative where it has to be (a label shared with a non-empty region,
or one the legacy dict predates, is kept) because a missing label would drop
that class entirely. Preprocessing now records present_labels after
modify_seg_fn, so the hint describes the segmentation the sampler actually
reads.
Write the store with several threads. _cparams pinned nthreads=1, so every
coordinate from the worker pool funnelled through one serial ZSTD-9
compressor: 11.09 s…

title: Point the legacy usage and extension docs at the preprocessed data format reference
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
how_to_use_nnunet.md and extending_nnunet.md are the pre-Diataxis twins of pages
that were already updated. Both describe the preprocessed folder / extension
points without mentioning the foreground sampling location store, which matters
for custom preprocessors because locations are now extracted after modify_seg_fn.
(cherry picked from commit fb99ab91d93a9d00458a96a836f821236fbbcf6c)

title: Store foreground sampling locations in a compressed per-configuration store
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
properties['class_locations'] kept every foreground sampling coordinate in each
case's pkl as an (N, 4) int64 array. The dataloader needs at most one coordinate
per patch, but had to read and unpickle the whole file to get it. On datasets
with many classes this dominated dataloading IO and disk usage: on
TotalSegmentator v2 (1228 cases, 117 classes) the pkl files totalled 18.26 GB,
28% of the preprocessed folder and 76x more than every segmentation combined.
Coordinates now live in one blosc2 store per configuration folder, addressed by
a CSR index. A lookup memory-maps a handful of index values and decompresses a
single block. Sampling behaviour is unchanged - the same
_sample_foreground_locations runs with the same parameters, and the store was
verified to reproduce the legacy coordinate sets exactly (520 case/class pairs,
856,754 coordinates on Hippocampus, zero mismatches).
Format, chosen by measurement on real TotalSegmentator coordinates:
 - flat linear uint64 indices, sorted within each (case, class) run. Sorting is
 worth 4x; uint64 compresses to the same size as uint32 after the filters, so
 there is no voxel-count ceiling. (N, 3) uint16 is 2.8x worse.
 - ZSTD-9 with [SHUFFLE, BYTEDELTA]: 0.72 B/coord vs 1.69 unfiltered.
 - chunks of 8192, blocks of 512. Compression ratio follows the block size;
 chunk size only matters via blocks per chunk.
 - reads via schunk[i:i+1] rather than NDArray[i] (4-5x faster; valid because
 the array is 1D).
 - CSR index as plain mmapped…

title: Deduplicate ResEncUNetPlanner; use assemble_plan in it
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
resencUNet_planner.py held a second, independently maintained copy of
ResEncUNetPlanner. Since -pl resolves planners by name and takes the first
match while walking the package tree, `-pl ResEncUNetPlanner` picked up that
stale copy while nnUNetPlannerResEncM/L/XL derived from the maintained one in
residual_unets/, so the bare planner and its own presets could drift apart.
The two had already diverged by one line (np.minimum vs an elementwise min
when clipping the initial patch size to the median shape, which differ in
dtype). resencUNet_planner.py is now a re-export with a DeprecationWarning,
so both import paths and the -pl lookup all yield the same class.
ResEncUNetPlanner.get_plans_for_configuration also duplicated the 22-line
plan-dict tail verbatim from ExperimentPlanner: the three determine_* calls
plus the 15-key configuration dict. It now ends in self.assemble_plan(...),
so the plan schema has a single source and adding a key to it can no longer
silently skip the ResEnc planners.
No behaviour change. Verified by regenerating plans before and after and
diffing: ExperimentPlanner, ResEncUNetPlanner and nnUNetPlannerResEncM/L/XL on
Datasets 003 and 027 are byte-identical (10 files), and since `-pl
ResEncUNetPlanner` now resolves to a different class, that one was checked
separately on Datasets 002, 004, 005, 010 and 017 as well - the legacy and
maintained implementations emit identical plans there too.

title: Support list-valued arch kwargs; factor out assemble_plan
author: Fabian Isensee
text:
get_network_from_plans: entries of arch_kwargs_req_import may now be a
list/tuple of import strings, not just a single one, so an architecture can
take a per-stage kwarg such as one residual block class per resolution stage.
Previously pydoc.locate was handed the whole list and returned None. Each
distinct string is resolved once and cached, since per-stage lists usually
repeat the same class. Scalar and None values behave exactly as before. This
is the single instantiation choke point, so the fix covers training,
inference and the VRAM estimator alike.
ExperimentPlanner.assemble_plan: the configuration-dict construction moves out
of get_plans_for_configuration into its own method. Planners for
fixed-capacity architectures - those that pin their own patch size, batch size
and topology instead of deriving them from a VRAM budget - can now reuse the
exact plan schema rather than duplicating the dict. Pure refactor.
Also adds nnUNetTrainer_2epochs next to the 1- and 5-epoch debug trainers.
Verified: regenerating nnUNetPlans and nnUNetResEncUNetLPlans on Dataset003
before and after this change gives byte-identical plans (modulo the plans_name
used to keep the two runs apart); a stock ResEnc-L still builds from plans at
102.35 M params with 5 DS heads; and a plan whose `block` kwarg is a 6-entry
list now builds the intended BasicBlockD/BottleneckD mix instead of failing.
Needs dynamic-network-architectures with per-stage block support for that
second case.

text:

- missing best checkpoint
- the normal training + `--val_best` path

Fixes #3056

title: Scope intel_macos extra constraints to macOS via platform marker
author: mark-rustad
text:
## Problem
The `intel_macos` optional-dependency group pins `torch<2.3` and `numpy<2` **without an environment marker**:
intel_macos = [
"torch<2.3",
"numpy<2", …
Because the group is opt-in, this is harmless for a plain `pip install nnunetv2`. But in resolvers that solve **all extras together** against a single universal lock — e.g. **uv workspaces** (common when nnU-Net is vendored as an editable submodule) or pip-tools universal resolution — the caps participate in the resolution for *every* platform. The unmarked `torch<2.3` then leaks onto non-macOS hosts and silently holds torch at `2.2.x` even on Linux/CUDA machines that opted into **no** extras.
Concretely, on a Linux + A100 (CUDA 12.8) host this forces `torch 2.2.2+cu121` / `torchvision 0.17.2` / `numpy 1.26.4` and the 2023-era `…

title: Fix UnboundLocalError when passing a dict to load_checkpoint
author: vcasellesb
text:
### Description
This PR fixes a bug in `nnUNetTrainer.load_checkpoint` where passing a checkpoint as a dictionary (as permitted by the `Union[dict, str]` type hint) results in an `UnboundLocalError`. 
Previously, if a dictionary was passed, the `isinstance(filename_or_checkpoint, str)` block was skipped, leaving the local variable `checkpoint` undefined before the subsequent `for` loop attempted to iterate over `checkpoint['network_weights']`.
### The Fix
Renamed the input argument from `filename_or_checkpoint` to `checkpoint`. 
* If a `str` is passed, it loads the file and correctly overwrites the `checkpoint` variable.
* If a `dict` is passed, it bypasses the string check and seamlessly falls through to the rest of the function using the provided dictionary.
This fix was applied to both…

This PR adds a small opt-in utility for training deep ensemble members using nnU-Net’s existing fold infrastructure.

title: [FIX] patch sampling in get_bbox() method to ensure patches are always fully contained inside the volume when oversampling foreground
author: sifaoso
text:
Hey all,
Thanks a lot for all the work that has gone into nnU-Net over the years!
I believe I found a bug in patch sampling when visualizing 3D CT batches (AMOS dataset), where some sampled patches contain slices outside the scan field-of-view (resulting in unexpected padding).
The issue occurs in the `get_bbox()` method when `force_fg=True` (foreground oversampling). However, when constructing the patch, the resulting bounding box is only constrained with respect to the lower bounds (`lbs`) and is not checked against the upper bounds (`ubs`), which define the valid sampling range to keep the patch fully inside the volume (here: https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet/blob/e73…

title: fix copying dataset.json to `output_folder` in `ensemble_folders` function
author: hxviet
text:
This fix changes how the dataset.json file is written to the output folder.
The old implementation tries to copy the file at the path `join(list_of_input_folders[0], 'dataset.json'`. When `dataset_json_file_or_dict` is specified, the file at this path is probably not intended to be used by `ensemble_folders` or may not even exist. The new implementation dumps the `dataset_json` object instead to ensure `ensemble_folders` writes the correct dataset.json data to the output folder whether `dataset_json_file_or_dict` is None, a file path, or a dictionary.

title: fix: remove HTTP/1.0 override that breaks Zenodo model downloads
author: github-actions[bot]
text:
Fixes #2876
## What was broken
`nnunetv2/model_sharing/model_download.py` forced HTTP/1.0 by overriding `http.client.HTTPConnection._http_vsn` and `_http_vsn_str`. Zenodo (and many modern services) requires HTTP/1.1 for proper redirect handling. The HTTP/1.0 override caused Zenodo to return `404 Not Found` instead of redirecting to the actual file download URL, making `nnUNetv2_download_pretrained_model_by_url` unusable.
## What this fixes
Removes the three lines that forced HTTP/1.0. The `requests` library uses HTTP/1.1 by default and handles Zenodo's redirects correctly without any override.
## How to verify
Run `nnUNetv2_download_pretrained_model_by_url` with a valid Zenodo URL — it should now successfully download and install the model instead of failing with a 404 error.

title: fix: use shutil.copyfile to avoid permission error on shared output dirs
author: github-actions[bot]
text:
Fixes #2882
## What was broken
`shutil.copy()` in `nnUNetTrainer.on_train_start()` (line 972) copies both file content **and** permission bits (via `chmod`). When multiple Linux users share the same output directory, the second user's training fails with `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted` because `chmod` requires file ownership — even if the directory has group write permissions.
## What this fixes
Replaces `shutil.copy()` with `shutil.copyfile()`, which copies **only the file content** without attempting to modify permissions. The permission bits of `dataset_fingerprint.json` are irrelevant — only the JSON content matters.
## How to verify
1. As user A, run training that creates `dataset_fingerprint.json` in the output folder
2. As user B (same group, shared directory w…

title: fix: avoid passing None chunks/blocks to blosc2.asarray
author: github-actions[bot]
text:
Fixes #2838
## What was broken
`nnUNetDatasetBlosc2.save_seg()` always passed `chunks=chunks_seg, blocks=blocks_seg` to `blosc2.asarray`, even when both were `None`. Newer versions of blosc2 (>=3.6.0) reject explicitly-passed `None` values for `chunks`/`blocks` and raise `RuntimeError: Could not build empty array`, whereas older versions (<=3.5.x) silently accepted `None` and computed defaults internally.
This broke the cascade training pipeline, where `save_seg` is called from `export_prediction.py` without providing `chunks_seg` or `blocks_seg`.
## What this fixes
Only passes `chunks` and `blocks` kwargs to `blosc2.asarray` when they are not `None`, letting blosc2 use its own defaults otherwise. This is compatible with both old and new blosc2 versions.

title: Use safetensors in addition to python pickle files (.pth) for tensors and metadata
author: mhalle
text:
## Summary
Replaces nnU-Net's `.pth` pickle checkpoints with a self-describing safetensors layout, with a backwards-compatible dual-write so existing tooling keeps working.
## Why
nnU-Net's existing code calls `torch.load(..., weights_only=False)` everywhere it loads a checkpoint. As of PyTorch 2.6 the default is `weights_only=True`, and **CVE-2025-32434** (CVSS 9.3, fixed in 2.6.0) demonstrated remote code execution through `torch.load` even with `weights_only=True`. nnU-Net checkpoints contain optimizer state and arbitrary `init_args`, so every legacy load takes the unsafe path. Distributing pretrained `.pth` models to third parties is now distributing a known attack vector.

batchgeneratorsv2>=0.3.0

So the minimum required `batchgeneratorsv2` version should likely be bumped (`batchgeneratorsv2` will need a new release too).

text:
Fixes #2729 (partial — isolating the double .get() fix as requested by @FabianIsensee)
## Problem
In `default_preprocessor.py`, worker results were being fetched twice using `.get()`:
# First call — consumes the result
_ = [r[i].get() for i in done]
# Second call — waits forever for a result already consumed …
The second `.get()` call would hang indefinitely waiting for a result 
that was already consumed by the first call, causing silent freezes 
during preprocessing.

for i in done:
r[i].get() # trigger any errors from worker (single call, no duplicate)
pbar.update()

title: Added command line argument `--not_on_device` to disable `perform_everything_on_device` during inference.
author: ancestor-mithril
text:
* Enabling `--not_on_device` ensures sliding window aggregation is performed on cpu. 
* This feature is usefull for inference on GPUs without enough VRAM (e.g. CTs with more than 1000 slices might not fit in 8GB VRAM)
* Without this feature, the default inference pipeline tries to do everything on GPU (`perform_everything_on_device=True`) and falls back to the CPU device only after failure (which might take some time). Moreover, the gaussian heatmap remains allocated on the CUDA device due to the lru_cache.
Commits: Added command line argument to disable computation on the full 3d volume on cuda device

text:

The `imagecodecs` package was listed as a dependency in `pyproject.toml`

- Successfully installed and ran nnUNet without `imagecodecs`

title: Keys in channel names ignored
author: stefan-kuczera-gu
text:
Keys in channel_names in dataset.json file are not considered. For example
"channel_names": {
"1": "noNorm",
"2": "T2", …
gives exactly the same preprocessing result as 
"channel_names": {
"f": "noNorm",
"l": "T2", …
Relevant line in code https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet/blob/8c4184d46b60059ff7dc8f74cd535e13554bdeca/nnunetv2/experiment_planning/experiment_planners/default_experiment_planner.py#L204

you are right, this is indeed the case. However, this is actually intended, as it maps the name of the channel to a normalization scheme (check [here](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet/blob/master/documentation/explanation_normalization.md?plain=1#L20)). This can be importan…
stefan-kuczera-gu: @ykirchhoff 
It would be nice to state more clearly in the documentation that the **_keys_** in channel_names are not processed and thus have no relevance while the **_values_** have to be in the same order as the input data channels.

title: Save memory usage during inference using recent PyTorch versions
author: Shrajan
text:
Hi nnUNet team and users,
`Line 138` in `nnunetv2/utilities/label_handling/label_handling.py` contains `logits = logits.float()` which doubles memory consumption during inference (validation and testing) . The original rationale for this conversion was added because "softmax, etc. is not implemented for half", which is true for older PyTorch versions (if I remember correctly, for torch<2.2.0).
#### Suggested Solution
You can either comment out `line 138`, or consider adding a PyTorch version check to conditionally apply this conversion only when necessary:
if torch.__version__ < "2.2.0": # or whatever the minimum version is
logits = logits.float()
So far, I have not observed any accuracy degradation after removing the conversion.
vmiller987: I will look at this as I have slightly larger than average CT scans. Thanks for sharing, hopefully this helps.
vmiller987: @Shrajan Does this happen during `nnUNetv2_predict`? I'm currently trying to test out your suggestion, but the predict does not get to this line for me.
Shrajan: @vmiller987 You are correct. This is not used if you do regular training and not apply `softmax`. But if you do `region-based` training or run inference with `save_probabilities` argument, then it will be used.

title: Determinism implementation in nnunet
author: Luugaaa
text:
Hi MIC-DKFZ team,
This PR introduces updates to enable fully deterministic training in nnU-Net, which is crucial for reproducibility in research. Achieving deterministic behavior in a multi-process environment can be tricky. Even with seeding, sources of randomness can persist, especially in the data augmentation pipeline. title: Just a Suggestion!
author: ananyaananth29
text:
## Feature Request: GUI for nnU-Net (Graphical User Interface)
While discussing nnU-Net with a colleague, we realized that there is currently no graphical user interface (GUI) for the tool. This inspired the idea of developing a GUI to make nnU-Net significantly more accessible — especially for medical researchers, clinicians, and domain experts who may not have programming expertise.

title: Fixed a bug in preprocessing in crop_to_nonzero. #2796
author: kreininmv
text:
Hi! 
#2796 
I’ve identified the root cause of the issue. In `preprocessing.preprocessors.default_preprocessor`, the function `crop_to_nonzero` is called to generate a `nonzero_mask` of the image and crop to the region of interest—but that region is defined as every non-zero pixel in the image. Clearly, that’s not correct: any voxel inside the patient can be non-zero, and manufacturer-specific differences in CT scanner background intensity mean the background is almost never exactly zero.
I see several possible solutions:
1. **Swap the preprocessing steps**: run `normalize` first, then `crop_to_nonzero`. However, this has drawbacks: if users have already cropped tightly around an organ or body region, the mask may over-crop and break training. Moreover, the CT normalization used doesn’t ze…

I believe however that there are some thins you did not interpret quite right, leading to the perception there is a bug or unintended behavior. I have already written a short response outlining the need for the nonzero mask in the issue you link to, h…
FabianIsensee (maintainer): Hey, I think there is a misunderstanding on what this nonzero area is supposed to be and what it is doing in nnU-Net
- the nonzero area is _not_ intended as a ROI segmentation in the sense that it should segment the body in a CT scan. It is a heuristic that should cut out non-informative and empty…

title: Bugfix - predict_from_data_iterator tensor serialization issue
author: Kenneth-Schroeder
text:
I have encountered several fatal SIGBUS errors using TotalSegmentator which uses nnUnetV2 under the hood. 
The errors occurred when running TotalSegmentator on large inputs.
After some digging, I was able to boil the issue down to the predict_from_data_iterator function of nnUNet, which passes the (in my case quite large) prediction result tensors to worker processes. For this step, the tensors need to be serialized, which apparently can cause memory alignment issues and trigger SIGBUS errors.
I noticed the error would disappear if I removed the multiprocessing logic, but numpy arrays seem much more stable regarding serialization and fixed the SIGBUS errors even with multiprocessing, hence this PR.
Here's a summary from Claude AI with slightly more details:
# SIGBUS Error in PyTorch Multi…
Commits: remove .copy(), keep .detach() as reminder even though it is probably not needed either; increase minor version and add .copy() for safety; fix memory alignment issues with large tensor serialization in predict_from_data_iterator
FabianIsensee (maintainer): Hey Kenneth, thanks for the PR! And sorry for being late. I have too many responsibilities and can impossibly keep up with everything.
I merged your changes, but am not happy with changing from tensor to array. We communicate tensors for a reason. They can be transferred between processes MUCH fast…

title: apply_inference_nonlin after averaging probabilities

text:

Here's what I came up with:
- When we call `nnUNetv2_predict` with `--save_probabilities` inference non-linearity layer is applied and what is stored in the `.npz` files are probabilities and not logits
- Probabilities coming from different models are averaged
- `label_manager.convert_logits_to_segmentation` is called instead of `label_manager.convert_probabilities_to_segmentation` because after averaging in the multiclass case, you can have the sum of the probabilities for a voxel that is not 1. text:
I have developed a model for medical image segmentation using training data with an out-of-plane voxel size of 3 mm. The in-plane voxel size is just below 1 mm (50 cm/512 voxels = 0.977 mm). title: Inquiry About CUDA Out of Memory Issue in nnUNet
author: CYYJL
text:
Dear Developer,
I am reaching out regarding an issue I encountered while developing an algorithm in nnUNet. Specifically, I am facing a seemingly counterintuitive problem. My model has only 0.2M parameters, whereas nnUNet and UMamba have 58M and 117M parameters, respectively. However, when performing BrainTumour segmentation, I encountered the following error: `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 20.00 MiB. GPU`

title: Specify Dependency Versions in pyproject.toml to avoid future break in installation
author: mi-homes
text:
First of all, thanks for maintaining this awesome project! 🙌
I noticed that the pyproject.toml does not specify exact versions for some dependencies. While this allows flexibility, it can also lead to unexpected installation issues if a future release of a dependency introduces breaking changes. We recently experience this when a new release of pytorch 2.6 available breaking our installation.
Suggestion
To improve installation stability, I suggest specifying exact or compatible dependency versions in pyproject.toml, such as:
torch==2.5.1
This ensures that users can install the package reliably while still allowing minor updates.
Would you be open to adding this? I'd be happy to contribute a PR if needed.
Thanks again for your work! 🚀

title: adding focal loss, distance map dice loss, loading distance maps
author: andy-s-ding
text:
Added a FocalLoss class that also works in compound loss functions. nnUNet also currently does not have a framework for loading in distance maps that were calculated offline. I propose a framework of calculating distance maps from segmentations in the `preprocessed` folder designated by the `plans` json. These maps are saved as `<case_num>_dist.npy`. In doing so, the `plans` json does not need to necessarily be modified. I have also made a Dataset class and a DataLoader class that is able to load these distance maps during training. title: Fix dataset order in move plans command
author: PaulBrachmann
text:
Since the target dataset has been planned before and its plans should be applied to the pretraining dataset, not the other way around, the two dataset arguments should be swapped.
E.g., the following yields the expected behavior with `30` being the pretraining and `31` the target dataset:
nnUNetv2_move_plans_between_datasets -s 31 -t 30 -sp nnUNetPlans -tp preTrainingPlans

title: Implement Argmax Inference Instead of Softmax when 'has_regions' is False
author: PengchengShi1220
text:
Issue: I have encountered a memory consumption issue in my Docker setup during inference tasks. Specifically, when the shm-size is set to 30GB, the system can successfully process softmax operations on input tensors of size [24, 724, 435, 435]. However, reducing the shm-size to 15GB leads to the unexpected termination of the Docker container due to insufficient shared memory during softmax computation.
Solution: Implement argmax instead of softmax when the 'has_regions' flag is set to False. This change is intended to address the shared memory (shm-size) constraints within Docker environments. It has been observed that the Docker container can handle the computation effectively, even with the shm-size set to 0, after making the proposed change.

if self.dataloader_train is not None and \

self.dataloader_train._finish() …

title: fix: make sure that a custom output folder for cv results is empty
author: mzenk
text:
Issue:
When using `nnUNetv2_accumulate_crossval_results` and specifying an _existing_ output folder with argument `-o`, the specified folder is first deleted completely and re-created before CV results are saved in it. This is unexpected behavior and might need to undesired data loss.
Fix:
Require the directory specified with `-o` to be non-existent or empty.
Comment on alternative solution:
Another option would be to remove the `shutil.rmtree` in `nnunetv2/evaluation/accumulate_cv_results.py`, but this would affect the case where `-o` is not specified in the `nnUNetv2_accumulate_crossval_results` entrypoint. To keep the changes minimal, the `rmtree` command is kept as is.
Commits: fix: make sure that a custom output folder for cv results is empty
FabianIsensee (maintainer): Good find, much appreciated!

title: Adding sequential inference
author: ancestor-mithril
text:
## Changing the implementation of `predict_single_npy_array` from parallel to sequential.
By default, using `predict_single_npy_array` uses `PreprocessAdapterFromNpy` which creates an additional process for loading the data. This process is not needed because the data was already read into a npy array and is passed to nnUNet. This is also faster because Tensors do not need to be transferred between processes. 
`predict_single_npy_array` does not benefit from parallelism in any situation and the users would benefit more for being able to parallelize themselves `predictor.predict_single_npy_array`.
## Adding support for sequential prediction from files
This allows running `nnUNetv2_predict` with a single process. This allows using less RAM usage per `nnUNetv2_predict` and better paralleliza…

seziegler (maintainer): Hi @hwanython ,

title: Anyone investigated prediction performance of 5-fold versus 1-fold, with tta and without?

title: For tooth segmentation from CBCT(labeling issue)
author: deepsea6034625
text:
Now, I'm trying to make automatically tooth segmentation network from CBCT nii images.
And the main problem is that teeth label is very various.
As you know, in cii image, background is 0.
But in ground truth, labels for teeth is different.
For example, some label images labels are 1, 2, 3, 4, ..., 32
But in some images, labels are 1, 10, 11, 12, ..., 51.
And even in some images, labels are 1.21e3, 1.41e3,...
How can I segment tooth with this dataset?
deepsea6034625: Also problem is that teeth order is different in every images.
sten2lu: Hi @deepsea920415,
nnU-Net can only be trained on datasets where an identical label is used for each pattern.
E.g.
- incisor tooth is always label 1 
- molar tooth is always label 2
Therefore you need to change the ground truth annotations to reflect that.
Best regards

What would you say is the advantage of `@torch.inference_mode()` over `with torch.no_grad()`? Prediction speed seems to be the same

title: Question about why the default resampling uses order 3
author: ancestor-mithril
text:
In the `determine_resampling` function , `resampling_data_kwargs["order"]` is 3, which stands for bi-cubic interpolation. 
Why is tricubic interpolation used for resampling 3D volumes instead of trilinear interpolation? Does it have better results if the model is used to 3 cubic interpolated patches? 
Using trilinear interpolation is significantly faster, so I wonder why tricubic interpolation was chosen for nnUNet.
constantinulrich (maintainer): Hi, yes bi-cubic interpolation can gets better results. But if you have a CPU bottleneck you could also switch to trilinear interpolation. There will only be a minimal performance drop
constantinulrich (maintainer): Did this help? Can i close the issue?
constantinulrich (maintainer): Hi, we did not test it on a level of a publication, but quite rigorous across some datasets and observed minimal performance drop. 
However, we are also testing pytorch resampling at the moment which improves speed and memory consumption a lot, but comes with a minimal performance drop as well...
ancestor-mithril: Sure, you can close the issue anytime. 
I am just wondering whether you know of some study / paper which analyses the performance drop from using trilinear vs tricubic interpolation.

author: ancestor-mithril

This feature allows to do fewer iterations of pseudo-validation instead of 50, allowing for faster training or more confident pseudo-validation score, depending on the needs of each experiment. title: New feature: adding a parameter to control the number of processes used by the validation dataloader
author: ancestor-mithril
text:
## Motivation
Many nnUNet users try to run it on systems in which the hardware is lacking (there are many users reporting `Some background worker is 6 feet under`). 
Currently, the validation dataloader uses half the number of processes of the training dataloader. A default training with nnUNet uses 1 main process + 12 train dataloader processes + 6 validation dataloader processes, which copy all the main's process allocated memory. 
On systems with modest RAM resources, if there is enough RAM utilization during training, the validation dataloaders' memory (including the validation data that was already loaded) is moved on the swap partition because the validation dataloaders sleep and wait for the end of the training epoch, which makes the start of the validation very slow. 
Reducing the…

text:

> SimpleITK and numpy indexing access is in opposite order!
> 
> SimpleITK: image[x,y,z]
> numpy: image_numpy_array[z,y,x]
Becaus…

Currently deepsupervision is half-static in the code and is annoying to turn on/off.

title: Veretebrae mislabeling from 2D Xray images
author: karllandheer
text:
Hello, thank you very much for your package. I have used it in a variety of applications, usually to great success. The current task I am working on is segmenting lumbar vertebrae from 2D Xray images. Most of the time (~80%) the segmentations are essentially perfect. The remaining 20% or so there's either the issue of all vertebrae labelings are shifted up or down by one, or some vertebrae are essentially cut in two between two labelings (one correct, one incorrect). The ground truth segmentations have been verified by a radiologist. I was wondering if anyone had any similar experience and suggestions? The images are being split into roughly 4 patches, I was considering creating the patch size as the entire image to include more global context. Any other ideas?
Karol-G: Hello @karllandheer,
Thank you for utilizing nnU-Net and for bringing this issue to our attention.
To better understand and address the segmentation discrepancies you’re encountering in approximately 20% of cases, we kindly ask you to share some example images illustrating the problem. Specifically…
Karol-G: The problem was resolved by increasing the patch size to ensure that the model receives enough global context within each patch. This way the model was able to determine the location of every class more reliably.

title: Move package metadata to `pyproject.toml`
author: MathijsdeBoer
text:
Modern Python development is starting to move to a unified [`pyproject.toml`](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/reference/build-system/pyproject-toml/) file as opposed to the various ways of defining package metadata.
This pull request replaces the old style `setup.cfg` and `setup.py` to this `pyproject.toml` format.
Functionality has not changed. `pip install -e .` still works as expected, as do the entrypoints:
(venv) PS D:\PythonProjects\nnUNet> nnUNetv2_train
nnUNet_raw is not defined and nnU-Net can only be used on data for which preprocessed (...)
(...)
I've also added an example set of optional developer dependencies, which can be installed using the square brackets at the end of the package name.
For local install:
(venv) PS D:\PythonProjects\nnUNet> pip install -e .[dev]
Commits: Move to pyproject.toml

title: About RAM utilization
author: Hikaryyy
text:
Hello, I noticed a phenomenon during the nnUNet prediction process that the storage process of the current file after the prediction process is completed and the prediction process of the next file is occurring simultaneously. This results in a sharp increase in RAM usage, and it will only recover to normal levels after the current file storage is completed. If the storage time of a certain file is too long, it will cause the next file to complete the prediction, and when preparing to enter the storage phase, the previous file has not yet finished storage, ultimately leading to RAM overflow and process death.
May I ask if there is any solution? I am currently using batch prediction of prediction files to avoid this issue
seziegler (maintainer): Hi @Hikaryyy , you can try to reduce the number of processes for preprocessing `--npp` and the number of processes for the segmentation export `--nps`. They both default to 3.

title: Avoid index error when `spacings_of_axes` limited
author: joshestein
text:
`spacing_of_axes` [is defined in reference to `valid_axes_for_pool`](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet/blob/master/nnunetv2/experiment_planning/experiment_planners/network_topology.py#L58). Since it is [possible for `valid_axes_for_pool` to be of a smaller length than `dims`](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet/blob/master/nnunetv2/experiment_planning/experiment_planners/network_topology.py#L54), we can run into an index out of range error when[ attempting to access a dimensionality index](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet/blob/master/nnunetv2/experiment_planning/experiment_planners/network_topology.py#L82) that does not exist within `spacing_of_axes`.
This (small) change adds a check to see if we are out of bounds for `spaces_of_axes` and if so break.
FabianIsensee (maintainer): Hey, this is not the correct fix as the kernel sizes must be set for all dimensions. I fixed in in this commit: https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet/commit/33b27b106985d9514854b8053997f800ee8aebed
But nonetheless thanks a lot for your work. I really appreciate it!

for d in range(min(dim, len(spacing_of_axes))):

title: Voxel-wise importance weighting for training loss (eg, distance to boundary)
author: Thibescobar
text:

I'm wondering if there is an easy or not too tricky way to add a weight map to the data during training? To give more importance to some voxels than others, for example borders, small structures, or crucial regions in application cases. 
In Ronneberger's original paper for example, high weights are assigned to pixels located in areas where objects touch, thanks to distance-transform-based weighting.
This would also be interesting in tractography, where large vessels are easier to segment than small ones, but also more present, which could induce a convergence favoring large over small vessels.

title: Default num processes fix
author: joshestein
text:
A few small fixes:
1. The documentation for the default num processes for "2d" configuration species the num processes as 8, but was defaulting to 4.
2. Make the order of default num processes match the default order of the '-c' option (2d, 3d_fullres, 3d_lowres).
3. Since a set was used to store `np`, it would not allow duplicate num procceses. If we had (8, 4, 8), this would reduce to (8, 4), and there would subsequently be an [error thrown due to mismatching number of processes and number of configurations.](https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet/blob/master/nnunetv2/experiment_planning/plan_and_preprocess_api.py#L95)
Commits: Make dict order match default '-c' argument; Change `np` from set to array, allow duplicates; Update default_np for 2d to 8
FabianIsensee (maintainer): thanks!

title: In DDP mode, Fix the error of deleting the latest model at the end of training
author: lvguofeng
text:
In DDP mode, at the end of training, different processes will delete the latest model, causing some processes to enter the if statement, but when "os.remove" is executed, other processes have deleted the file, so an error "FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2 ] No such file or directory" will be reported.
Refer to the methods "save_checkpoint", "plot_progress", write the delete model as a function, under DDP, rewrite this function, just add "if self.local_rank == 0"

title: Deep supervision
author: TIAN-Ww
text:
The deep supervision mechanism of nnunet, the way to calculate the loss of depth supervision:1) is to process the Ground Truth into different scales, 2) or is to upsample the feature map of the current layer to restore it to the highest resolution.
FabianIsensee (maintainer): Thanks @thijsgelton !
thijsgelton: It downsamples the ground truth into depth - 1 increasingly smaller versions of the ground truth, such that spatially it corresponds to the output at each upsampling step. The loss is a weighted combination of the loss at each of these upsamples, starting with the lowest weight at the bottleneck + 1

title: best model maybe not right in multi-class segmentation
author: SummerZ2020
text:
Hi FabianIsensee, 
 thank you so much for your great work. it helps a lot. I found an issue about model_best save in multi_class segmentation. 
In my case, there is 2 kinds of foregrounds. the one is easy to recognize, let's say it is A, its metric is high, for example 0.9. The other one is difficult, let's say it is B, its metric is lower, for example 0.6. The mean metric is 0.75. But if B's metric is None sometime, and the mean metric is 0.9. it is higher than the normal mean metric. And the best model is saved in when B's metric is None, and it is can not be updated in later the normal iterations since the metric 0.9 is higher.
FabianIsensee (maintainer): Hey I see where this problem comes from. Unfortunately I don't see a good solution to this. What do you propose we do in this case? Simply not update the moving average?

FabianIsensee (maintainer): 0 = False positives were predicted (class was not present during validation) OR class was there and was not predicted
none = class was not present and no false positives were predicted
0.7 = class was there and was predicted
I recommend using the latest/final checkpoint anyways. Unless there is a r…

title: nnUNet_find_best_configuration generates wrong command example for ensembling model
author: VincentYCYao
text:
The command `nnUNet_find_best_configuration -m 2d 3d_fullres 3d_lowres 3d_cascade_fullres -t <task ID>` will generate a text file `<some paths>/nnUNet_trained_models/nnUNet/ensembles/<task name>/prediction_commands.txt` containing command example for model inference.

git clone https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet.git

best,
Fabian

I have already trained nnUNet for the task of chest-x-ray segmentation with ~190 training images of 1024x1024 without any problems, but I'm running into trouble when trying to run it on more bigger images. title: 2D better than 3D fullres
author: yilei-wu
text:
I have two datasets regarding the same type of task and ran nnUNet on both of them;
For dataset A (public), 3D full resolution solution is slightly better than the 2D solution. 
For dataset B (private), 2D solution outperform the 3D solution by around 8% dice score. (70% v.s. 62%)
I am not sure if it could be an indication of something wrong with my dataset B? The sanity check of nnunet data processing did not prompt me error but I am just feel it very uncommon since most of experiments listed in the supplemental material of the nnunet paper are seemed to achieve better performance with 3D solution. 
To put it in a more concise way:
Under what circumstance that 2D UNet may outperform 3D UNet ?
Thank you :)
FabianIsensee (maintainer): There was an old version of nnunet where this could happen (like years old, nothing recent) but we have since fixed this problem. On 3D datasets, the 3D configurations always work better or equally well as the 2D config. I don't know why this could be different for your dataset and I cannot really…
FabianIsensee (maintainer): @chrisrapson correct! Running all nnU-Net configurations is only really needed for users who don't know much about it (yet). Once you get a feeling for the datasets you will know what you'll need to run and what you can omit. For most 3D datasets I never run the 2D config.
Best,
Fabian

title: get_moreDA_augmentations segmentation resampling order parameter should be 0 (order_seg=0)
author: silvandeleemput
text:
The default `nnUNetTrainerV2` trainer uses the `get_moreDA_augmentation` method to setup the data generators.
https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/nnUNet/blob/96d44c2fc1ce5e18da4cd54bf52882047c37982e/nnunet/training/data_augmentation/data_augmentation_moreDA.py#L41-L46
However, the `get_moreDA_augmentation` method has the parameter for the resampling order for the segmentation masks set to `order_seg=1`. Shouldn't this be set to `order_seg=0` to use nearest neighbors resampling, which is typically used for segmentation mask resampling?
FabianIsensee (maintainer): nah order=1 is more accurate in my experience. There is no reason this has to be 0.
Note though that I don't really see a difference in segmentation performance between the two so you could also set it to 0 if you really desire (this would also reduce CPU utilization)
FabianIsensee (maintainer): This is long taken care of ;-) If you follow the code you will see it.
Segmentations are resampled by first converting them to a one-hot encoding. Then each encoding is resampled separately and finally the results are converted back to a segmentation map. No strange artifacts in nnU-net.
FabianIsensee (maintainer): From all those transforms only SpatialTransformWithWeights and SimulateLowResolutionTransform use interpolation and in there is the code you are looking for. The one hot encoding is only done temporarily during resampling. This is why you don't see it
silvandeleemput: Ah, I totally missed that, thanks for pointing it out!

title: number of patch sizes
author: wxr521314
text:
Hi，
 My data is in 3D. I want to know how many patches my data is divided into. My patch_size is 24x320x320. Can I understand that 24 represents the number of data layers? However, some of my data is less than 24 layers, how to do this?
Best wish！
FabianIsensee (maintainer): 24 represents the patch size in the first dimension. If your first dimension consists of layers then yes that's the layers. 
If the number of slices/layers is less than 24 nnU-Net will just pad the images. No problem with that.
nnU-Net does not explicitly create patches from your data. It just load…
FabianIsensee (maintainer): During preprocessing each image is processed as one, it is not divided into patches.
During training, an infinite number of random (!) patches is cropped from the preprocessed image.
Patches are never created and stored explicitly. This would be a waste of disk space due to redundant saving of some…
FabianIsensee (maintainer): Hey @beantr96, this is because the patch size must be a multiple of 2**num_pool. So if we want to pool 4 times along that axis, we cannot have 18 because that would result in a non-integer filter map size in the bottleneck. So we increase the patch size to the closest value that fulfills this requi…
wxr521314: So my data has only one patch to input into the prediction network?
